pool.coverWarning: Only do this if that poller can reach these devices: every node it cannot reach will report as down, just like a real outage.
pool.coverNoTarget: No other pool has a live poller, so there is nothing to stand in.

pool.deleteConfirm: Delete {{pool}}. Nothing references it, so no monitoring stops.

bus.title: Remote pollers

state.internalNote: only the poller on this host can connect
state.encryptedNote: pollers at other sites connect over TLS

bus.noSwitch: This switch is unavailable: the component that applies it is not running.
bus.outage: The bus, this server and the poller running here are all restarted, so monitoring stops for about a minute. A maintenance window is opened for you, and this page will disconnect while it happens.

names.label: Addresses remote pollers will dial
names.required: Give at least one address, or no site will be able to connect.

cert.absent: No certificate yet. One is generated automatically the next time this deployment starts.
cert.uncovered: Not covered by this certificate: {{names}}. Reissue it before those sites can connect.

warn.unreadable: The private key cannot be read — the encryption key has changed or been lost. Reissue the certificate, then give the new one to every site.
warn.expired: This certificate has expired. Remote pollers are already refusing to connect. Reissue it, then give the new one to every site.
warn.expiring: This certificate expires soon. Reissuing it means giving the new one to every site, so plan for it rather than waiting.

reissue.title: Reissue the bus certificate
reissue.afterward: Every site must be given the new certificate before it can reconnect.
reissue.failed: failed to reissue the bus certificate

enable.title: Accept remote pollers
enable.intro: Publishes the bus port with TLS and a password, so pollers at other sites can connect.

disable.title: Stop accepting remote pollers
disable.intro: Returns the bus to this host only. Every poller at another site stops connecting, and the nodes assigned to it stop being monitored.

handoff.title: Give this to the site
handoff.onceOnly: Shown once. It is not stored anywhere it can be read again.
handoff.restarting: The bus is being reconfigured now. This page will reconnect on its own once it comes back.

steps.title: Connect a site by hand
steps.s1: At the site, save the bus certificate to a file.
steps.s3: Dial one of the addresses under Valid for, using the bus URL from the dialog.

token.title: Bus token — {{id}}
token.sharedHint: This poller is admitted by the deployment-wide bootstrap secret, the same one every other poller without its own token uses.
token.reissueWarning: The site stops connecting the moment you do this, and starts again once it is running the new archive.
token.downloaded: Downloaded. The token is only in that file — it cannot be shown again.

host.label: Address this site will dial
host.hint: Leave empty for the bus certificate's address; any other must be one the certificate covers.

selfUpgrade.label: Install the site updater, so upgrading here upgrades this site too
selfUpgrade.info: The updater is a second container at the site with access to its Docker socket. Without it the site stays on its current version, and the site's own .env can switch it later.

move.title: Move {{id}}
move.cannot: This poller cannot be moved yet — it is offline, or its build is older than this feature. Upgrade it first.

move.takeNodesWhy_other: Monitoring continues. {{count}} nodes move to {{pool}} as well.
move.leaveNodesWhy_one: {{count}} node stops being monitored, and no alert will be raised for it, until a poller serves that pool again.
move.leaveNodesWhy_other: {{count}} nodes stop being monitored, and no alerts will be raised for them, until a poller serves that pool again.

l3.name: Interface addresses
l3.info: Which IP prefixes each device has an address in. The network map derives links from shared subnets.

arp.name: ARP / IPv6 neighbor cache
arp.info: Hosts each router has actually spoken to. It is the only source that can name a device nobody has added yet.
arp.warn: This walk reads a table sized by the network, so it adds load on busy switches.

routing.name: Routing adjacency (OSPF / BGP / routes)
routing.info: Devices peered or directly routed to each other, including links that share no subnet. The routing table is never walked.

media.name: Interface media type
media.info: The physical medium of each Ethernet port, shown in the Interfaces tab. Many devices do not report it.
